chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from the son of the sister of Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from his maternal uncle Al-Walid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, among the people is one whose sustenance has been placed in the sword, and among them is one whose sustenance has been placed in trade, and among them is one whose sustenance has been placed in his tongue.
ai.seo_question: What are the different types of sustenance (rizq) mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the divine distribution of sustenance (rizq) through three primary channels: martial strength, commercial enterprise, and eloquent speech or knowledge. In Shia scholarly tradition, this categorization underscores that livelihood is a matter of divine decree (qadr), encouraging believers to excel in their designated path while maintaining spiritual integrity. It reflects the holistic view of human endeavor, where physical, economic, and intellectual pursuits are all valid means of receiving God's provision.
